fix(duckduckgo): recover favicons indexed under www host (#629) (#631)

DuckDuckGo's ip3 icon service is keyed by exact hostname and only
normalizes www <-> apex for popular domains. Smaller sites (e.g.
chrisd.ca) are indexed under the single host their crawler saw, usually
the canonical `www.` redirect target, so the other variant 404s and the
provider drops a favicon it actually has.

Probe the requested host and, on a miss, retry the www-toggled variant,
returning whichever DuckDuckGo actually serves. Falls back to the primary
URL when neither is reachable so the domain race rejects it uniformly and
resolves via Google/microlink.

feat(bimi): resolve the logo a domain publishes in its BIMI record (#634)

* refactor(avatar): let a provider list fall back in tiers

A flat list races every provider and takes the first to answer, so the winner
is whoever is fastest rather than whoever is best. That is fine when every
provider answers the same question, and wrong when one of them answers a
different one.

A list may now be a list of tiers: a tier races as before, and the next one
only runs once every provider in it has failed. A flat list stays a single
tier, so nothing changes for the lists as they are declared today.

The Tangerine resolver also moves out of cacheable-lookup into its own module,
so record lookups can share the instance that address lookups already use.

* feat(bimi): resolve the logo a domain publishes in its BIMI record

Reads the record through bimi-url, over the DNS resolver and got stack the
rest of unavatar already uses, memoized in its own keyv namespace. The logo
host is published by the domain being looked up, so it goes through
isReservedIp the same way mastodon's server does.
